Register kernR's conditional mean embedding as a flexyBayes C7 conformer

Source: R/surrogate_conformers.R
register_kernr_surrogates.Rd

Makes method = "cme" available to fit_surrogate() by registering an adapter around kernR's fit_cme(). kernR's CME is a kernel linear smoother that yields a conditional mean but no predictive variance; the adapter supplies the standard linear-smoother predictive variance sigma^2 (1 + ||w||^2) (with sigma^2 = RSS / (n - tr(S)) from the in-sample smoother), so the emulator honours the C7 distribution-preserving <o>_sd requirement. The conditional-mean map stays kernR's; only the uncertainty quantification is added here – not a reimplementation.

Usage

register_kernr_surrogates()

Value

Invisibly, the registered method name ("cme").

Out-of-support gate

The smoother weights w(x*) are an approximate partition of unity wherever x* is supported by the design: sum(w) is close to 1 across the training design. With a bounded, decaying kernel every k(x*, x_i) tends to zero as x* leaves the design, so sum(w(x*)) tends to 0, the mean w(x*)'y decays to zero, and ||w(x*)||^2 decays to zero – which drives the reported sd down to its in-design floor sqrt(sigma^2). Ungated, the conformer would report an in-design-sized uncertainty on a fabricated mean at exactly the point where it knows least.

The conformer therefore records the weight mass across the training design at fit time and refuses to predict where the mass falls below weight_mass_frac (default 0.5) times the least-supported design point's mass, raising a classed fb_surrogate_cme_abstention condition that names the offending rows, their mass, and the floor. Pass weight_mass_frac (or an absolute weight_mass_floor) through fit_surrogate() to retune it, or weight_mass_floor to predict() to override it for one call; set the floor to 0 to disable the gate. The reference rff surrogate widens as declared off-design and is the named fallback for extrapolation.

Called opportunistically from .onLoad() when kernR is installed.

See also

register_surrogate(), fit_surrogate(), register_pesto_surrogates().

Examples

if (requireNamespace("kernR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  register_kernr_surrogates()
  set.seed(1)
  a <- runif(80, -2, 2)
  e <- fb_ensemble(
    params = data.frame(a = a),
    outputs = data.frame(y = sin(a) + rnorm(80, 0, 0.05)),
    provenance = list(source = "raw")
  )
  s <- fit_surrogate(e, method = "cme", lambda = 1e-2)
  predict(s, data.frame(a = 0.5))
  # far outside the design the conformer declines rather than guessing:
  tryCatch(
    predict(s, data.frame(a = 40)),
    fb_surrogate_cme_abstention = function(cnd) conditionMessage(cnd)
  )
}
#> [1] "the 'cme' surrogate declines to predict at 1 of the supplied point(s): the conditional-mean smoother carries a weight mass of 6.41e-258 there (row 1), below the out-of-support floor 0.434. On the training design the mass runs 0.867 to 1.004; as a point leaves the design the kernel evaluations decay to zero, the smoother mean collapses toward zero and the linear-smoother variance sigma^2 (1 + ||w||^2) collapses to its in-design floor -- a confident wrong answer. Emulate this region with fit_surrogate(method = \"rff\"), which widens off-design as declared, keep the prediction inside the design, or lower `weight_mass_floor` deliberately."
